stages.title: THEISM, DEISM, PANTHEISM AND PANENTHEISM
stages.terms: Classical theism treats God as the primary sustaining cause through which genuine secondary natural causes operate.
stages.mechanism: Classical theism treats God as the primary sustaining cause through which genuine secondary natural causes operate.
stages.consequence: Pantheism and panentheism are not synonyms.
stages.trap: Deism is not atheism: it affirms a creator but rejects continuing providential intervention.
stages.answer: God is a personal creator, distinct from the world but continuously sustaining and governing it.

stages.title: SPINOZA'S NOTION OF GOD
stages.terms: In Spinoza, a substance is "in itself and conceived through itself." Its existence and conception do not depend upon another thing.
stages.mechanism: God could not have chosen a fundamentally different world through arbitrary will.
stages.consequence: The analogy is limited: Spinoza's modes follow with metaphysical necessity, whereas ordinary waves are contingent physical events.

stages.title: ADVAITA VEDANTA'S NOTION OF GOD
stages.terms: Saguna Isvara is Brahman viewed through maya.
stages.mechanism: Isvara, jiva and world belong to the standpoint eventually sublated by non-dual knowledge. [QUALIFICATION] Therefore Advaita accommodates empirical theism, but its ultimate metaphysics is non-dual rather than personalistic theism.
stages.consequence: Sat-cit-ananda is not a collection of three finite qualities.
stages.trap: [QUALIFICATION] Isvara is not false in the sense of non-existent.
stages.answer: Nirguna (without limiting qualities) means Brahman (ultimate reality) is free from limiting, finite and relational qualities.

stages.title: RAMANUJA'S VISISTADVAITA NOTION OF GOD
stages.terms: Brahman is non-dual qualified by selves and matter - hence Visista-advaita, "qualified non-dualism.".
stages.mechanism: Brahman is non-dual qualified by selves and matter - hence Visista-advaita, "qualified non-dualism.".
stages.consequence: Visistadvaita is not halfway compromise; it is an organic theory of unity-in-difference.
stages.trap: Reality is one organic whole, but its internal distinctions are real.
stages.answer: Ramanuja accepts all three as real but denies that they are three independent substances.

stages.title: NYAYA'S NOTION OF GOD
stages.terms: [QUALIFICATION] Philosophical pressure remains: if karma already determines results, why is God required?
stages.mechanism: Therefore Nyaya does not teach creation ex nihilo or a real transformation of God into the world.
stages.consequence: Therefore Nyaya does not teach creation ex nihilo or a real transformation of God into the world.
stages.trap: God, selves, atoms, space and time are real; they are not appearances of one undifferentiated Absolute.
stages.answer: Isvara (Lord or personal God) is eternal, omniscient, omnipotent and a special self never subject to bondage or karma (morally consequential action).

stages.title: THE HINDU POLYTHEISM DEBATE
stages.terms: Final verdict: Comparison is strongest when each position is judged through the same axes of ultimate reality, world relation, human relation, causation and religious function.

stages.title: MADHVA, SAIVA AND SAKTA NOTIONS OF GOD
stages.terms: Answer-grabbing line: Indian theism ranges from Madhva's eternal difference through Śaiva Lord-soul-bond structures to Śākta identity of divinity and power; none can be reduced to a generic “Hindu God.”.
stages.mechanism: each school connects a causal doctrine to bondage and liberation
stages.consequence: real difference, real manifestation and divine power replace Advaita's sublatable appearance
stages.trap: do not merge Śaiva Siddhānta with Kashmir Śaivism or reflection with identity
stages.answer: A complete core answer can therefore choose Śaiva Siddhānta or Madhva instead of using Rāmānuja every time.

stages.title: COMPARATIVE GOD-WORLD-MAN RELATIONS
stages.terms: Merely naming attributes does not explain what a God-concept philosophically entails.

stages.title: PHYSICAL MANIFESTATION AND ULTIMATE CAUSATION
stages.terms: Some God-concepts involve embodiment, but it is not conceptually necessary for every ultimate cause.
